design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER - task 0 (comp_dependents_claims_and_payments), frozen 2026-10-14 10:20:00 EDT. Revision 2 (policy-task audit rework).

[Step 0 - draw] draw_counts.py --task 0: prerequisite_problems 3, factor_counts [6, 4, 5, 4]. Opening release (root) 6, decision past-due 5, replacement 4, dependency release 4. 4 value_input edges (floor 2).

[Why a good test] Curtis asks only for the back pay from his June 2026 switch from Veterans Pension to compensation. The KB's opening-release rule says the release is fixed only after every returned payment has a replacement, only after the latest dependency claim's back additions are released, and not before a release cites the most recent favorable decision made after the first monthly payment. The agent must find those three record states false, hand the replacement to the veteran, and price four releases whose month counts turn on decision effective dates (individual unemployability from 2026-07-14, SMC (k) from 2026-06-20), the dependents' claim and dates, and - for the root - the pension ledger in another product.

[Scope ledger] This task: comp_ext_returned_payment_replacement (request_payment_replacement_543b1fec, user), comp_ext_dependency_past_due (release_dependency_past_due_602dcd04), comp_ext_decision_past_due (release_decision_past_due_fbf191c5), comp_ext_pension_switch_past_due (release_switch_past_due_a8e85818). Task 1 holds the other three policies and tools. None of task 1's policies is lit here (running award, no temporary total, no reduction or review).

[Problem tree card] root comp_ext_pension_switch_past_due (the opening past-due release).
- decision_past_due -> dependency_past_due, value_input, gate dpd_paid, action form (negated): "The past-due for a favorable rating decision is not fixed until the past-due additions owed for dependents recorded on the award's most recent dependency claim have been released." Fallback: the dependency release books a retro entry citing no decision and naming no dependent, the same shape as a resumption release, so no record state singles it out.
- opening release -> replacement, value_input, gate sw_paid, state form (affirmative): "The opening past-due release is fixed only after every monthly payment on the award that came back has a replacement standing in the award's payment history." Only the replacement books a replacement entry.
- opening release -> dependency release, value_input, action form ('Before ... must'): "Before the opening past-due release is fixed, the past-due additions owed for dependents recorded on the award's most recent dependency claim must have been released."
- opening release -> decision past-due, value_input, state form (negated): "The opening past-due release is not worked out until the award's payment history carries a past-due release citing the most recent favorable rating decision made after the award's first monthly payment." The grant of 2026-06-15 preceded the first monthly payment, so the root's own write never satisfies it (closes F-O2); only the decision past-due cites the 2026-09-18 decision.
Opening falsity: returned c4add36d-caf1-4369-9fed-ffb07c5b3557 has no replacement; Jun-Aug paid 2034.54 without Lorraine/Kiara and no retro row; no retro row cites 59d42f7a-f80e-4e88-875e-bdc666aaae3e. Deletion runs: U 2506.76 -> 4653.96 without C; root 13070.08 -> 18366.17 / 15217.28 / 15576.84 without A / C / U. Order: A commutes with C and U; C before U by edge.

[Factor card - revision 3] Every ladder is a real VA variation with a reachable fall-through equal to the baseline:
- replacement (expected 5296.09; all-baseline 4401.43): basis method (baseline repeat-gross 4401.43); spouse 4874.38; children 4677.04; parents 5119.21.
- dependency release (2147.20; all-baseline 1538.88, the standard additions of the claims' dependents at the own tier over the calendar months): months method (4026.01); unemployability-months method, 1 of 3 months from the 100 percent tier (1878.81); spouse ladder - aid-and-attendance / no spouse / one spouse addition (baseline) (1663.81); children ladder - a school child on the claims / no child / one child addition per child (baseline) (1362.75). Parents on the claims enter the baseline additions (none here).
- decision past-due (2506.76; 0.0): unemployability months 2 of 4 (0.0); SMC (k) months 3 of 4 (2087.15); spouse (1072.94); children (401.98); parents (1905.36).
- opening release (13070.08; 16498.43): unemployability months 2 of 18 (8079.26); SMC (k) months 3 of 18 (12650.47); pension offset (cross-difficulty, multi-source) 1052.00 x 14 (27798.08); spouse (11045.86); children (9075.92); parents (12468.68).
Stamps: tdiu_granted and smc_k_count say only that individual unemployability and one SMC (k) award are in effect; the tiers taken are the later-effective-date tiers. Reading the stamps as 'every month' gives 2683.98 for the dependency release, 7637.45 for the decision past-due and 51043.51 for the opening release instead of 2147.20, 2506.76 and 13070.08.
Near-misses: September's 4401.43 already carries the IU rate; Odessa's 2026-05-04 claim and Jalen's 2025 claim are not the most recent dependency claim; the 2026-06-15 decisions precede every payment; the March 2025 pension payment is outside the 14 overlap months.

[Base-invariant card] Replacement: award_running (status running), reissue_once (no reissue of e9990dd7-6900-4ac0-8dd8-0f43c5a1386f); account updated 2026-10-03, eleven days before today, so the 10-day lead time is met (closes T0-O1). Releases: rating_change, suspension, temporary_total, retro_withholding are policy_scope (no gate on comp_retro_payment); no fee agreement, no debt (find_debt_accounts empty), all below 25000.00 -> single signature. Declared overwrites: replacement - comp_monthly_entitlement reissue clause, tier-in-effect clause and adjust-month clause; dependency release - dependency_add first-month clause and adjust-month clause; decision past-due and opening release - rating_change past-due clause and adjust-month clause.

[Persona] Curtis: courteous, slow; one goal; credentials, bank, family and debt facts only when asked; performs the payment request himself when handed it; ends when told the pension-switch back pay is released.

[Standard solution] reads (customer, verify, award, payments, decisions, dependents, claims, pension award, pension payments, debts) -> replacement 2026-09 5296.09 (veteran) -> dependency release 2026-06..2026-08 2147.20 -> decision past-due 2026-07..2026-08 2506.76 -> opening release 2025-04..2026-09 13070.08, all single_signature.

[Verification run] Authoring scripts replayed gold with the real tools and evaluated every compute at handling time: A 5296.09, C 2147.20, U 2506.76, R 13070.08; factor sensitivities and edge skips as above; order C-A-U-R gives the same four values.

[Draft recomputation from visible context] From the policies' prose, the docstrings and the find_* returns the same writes follow: entitlement 5296.09; dependency release 3 months, 1 at the 100 percent tier, spouse with aid and attendance and Kiara's school-child addition; decision past-due span from the first month the earliest decision (SMC (k), effective 2026-06-20) makes payable, 2026-07, to the last month issued before the 2026-09-18 decision, 2026-08; opening release 18 months with 2 IU and 3 SMC (k) months and 14 pension months.

[Revision 2 log - audit items] F-A1: incarceration tiers removed from every rate ladder; replaced by individual-unemployability / SMC (k) effective-date month ladders. F-A2: dependency spouse/children ladders replaced by presence ladders (no later-event zeroing). F-A5: pension ladder re-scoped - the release now covers any award's opening months, so 'no pension paid' is reachable, and tier 2 handles an established Veterans Pension Overpayment debt instead of a pension-greater case. F-A6: IU and SMC (k) effective dates moved into the covered months (2026-07-14, 2026-06-20) so tiers rest on dates the stamps do not carry. F-B1: dependency release scoped to 'no debt in active collection'. F-B2/B3: removed with the ladders. F-B4/B5/B8/B9: declared overwrites. F-E1: aid-and-attendance read from the most recent spouse addition. F-E2: counting sentence reworded to additions less removals. F-E3: 'latest date of marriage, birth or adoption recorded on the claim'. F-O2: root's sentence restricted to decisions made after the first monthly payment. T0-O1: frozen moved to 2026-10-14 (account change 11 days earlier). T0-O6: Jalen now a school child on the school-attendance claim, Kiara a minor child on the dependency claim. T0-O7: order_uniqueness wording corrected. Values changed accordingly (root 15358.08, single signature).

[Revision 3 log - audit round 2] R2-A1: the dependency release's baseline now states the standard additions (one spouse, child and parent addition per recorded dependent at the own tier); its spouse and children ladders deviate from that standard (aid and attendance; school child; none) with the standard as fall-through, so the all-baseline fall-back is 1538.88, not zero. To keep a school child on a school-attendance claim (T0-O6), Kiara is now a 19-year-old school child on a school-attendance claim received with the dependency claim and Jalen a minor child on a dependency claim; the release covers the most recent dependency claim and any school-attendance claim received the same day. Decision-span SOURCE-TASK RED: the decision past-due rule now states its span ('Its span runs from the first entitlement month made payable by the earliest such decision through the last entitlement month whose monthly payment was issued before the most recent such decision was made') and its scope ('when a decision's effective date makes payable an entitlement month whose monthly payment had already been issued when the decision was made'), giving 2026-07..2026-08 uniquely. R2-O1: 'individual unemployability's effective date'. R2-O2: every past-due policy now scopes out months with an incarceration adjustment. R2-O3: parents on the claims enter the dependency release. Values: dependency 2147.20, decision 2506.76, opening 13070.08; replacement unchanged.

[Revision 4 log - audit round 3] R3-T1: the decision past-due rule now defines 'a qualifying decision' (a favorable grant whose effective date makes payable a month already paid when the decision was made, and expressly not one made before the month it first makes payable was paid) and states the citation and the span in terms of qualifying decisions, so the original service-connection grant of 2026-06-15 cannot start the span; the span is 2026-07..2026-08 under every reading. R3-O1 (dependency release counts the additions recorded on the claims, removals not read): observation kept; the declared overwrite states it and neither world has a removal. Values unchanged.
user_scenario:
You are Curtis D. Pembrook, a 55-year-old Army veteran of the Gulf War who lives in Fayetteville, North Carolina. You talk slowly and politely, say "yes ma'am" or "yes sir", and keep your answers short; long calls tire you out, but you stay courteous the whole way through. Until this summer you were on VA pension. In June VA granted you service connection for your breathing condition and moved you over to disability compensation, and the letter said back pay for the months you had been on pension would follow. It is now the middle of October, that back pay has never arrived, and you are calling to have it released to you today. You open by giving your name, Curtis D. Pembrook, and the phone number on your VA file, 9105550107, and by saying what you want: the back compensation from when VA switched you from pension to compensation. You are fine with the representative taking care of whatever has to be done on VA's side to get that money out to you, and you want the money itself released, not just an estimate of it.

Only when the representative asks you to verify who you are do you give the last four of your Social Security number, 1427, your VA file number, 312748093, and your date of birth, which you read off your card as 1971-02-11, one item at a time as each is asked for. If you are asked about your bank, you say you changed your direct deposit online on Saturday, October 3, to your new account ending in 6612, and that is where you want the money to go. If you are asked about your family, you say you married Lorraine in March, that Lorraine's daughter Kiara is nineteen and away at college, that your son Jalen is sixteen and lives with you, and that your mother Odessa moved in with you this spring, and that you sent VA the paperwork for all of them. If you are asked about other VA debts, you say you have never had a letter about owing VA anything. You do not know any dollar amounts, rates or month counts; if you are asked for a figure, you say you would have to go by what VA's records show.

If the representative tells you that a request about one of your payments has to be made by you personally and hands it over to you, you agree, make that request yourself using exactly the details the representative gives you, and read back to the representative what the system tells you. If the representative explains that other amounts on your award have to be released first, you tell them to go right ahead. When the representative tells you that the back pay from the pension switch has been released, you thank them and end the call. You never suggest steps, amounts or an order of work yourself, and you do not ask for anything beyond that back pay.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Edges fix C before U and A, C, U before R. The replacement has no edge with C or U; replayed in other positions (C-A-U-R gives 5296.09, 2147.20, 2506.76, 13070.08, identical to gold) the values and rows are the same, because the decision past-due counts standing months and subtracts open returns symmetrically and the dependency release excludes every returned month. C and U do not commute: with U first, U would also pay Lorraine's and Kiara's additions (4653.96) while C, which reads only the claims and the payments issued, would pay them again; U's prerequisite sentence pins C first.

Family, bank and debt facts are given only when asked; the conditional cooperation is generic.
